items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The French jazz fans and those in many other countries are not too wild about singers in jazz groups unless it's Pops Armstrong, Ella Fitzgerald, or some one in a group that can remind the fans of certain jazz or blues singers.

ctx.x: The president of the Hot Club was there to meet us because he knew when we would return to Marseilles. He gave me a message from Tommy which was that he was waiting for us. I gave him one to take back to Tommy which was that he could keep waiting.

We finished the rest of the tour which was eight more concerts ending in Dijon the 14th of December. The tour had been a booking success for Lily who three years before, had not known anything about jazz and had arranged her first tour one year before this one. Without Tommy the rest of the tour continued to make a hit whereever we played and we could have saved more money than we did if the whole tour had been done without a singer. I had a contract for 10 days as the Casino Rosatsch in S. Moritz. Left Paris the 20th of December and opened the 22nd. Bill Tamper stayed in Paris as my contract was for five musicians. From there I went to S. Gallen, still in Switzerland at the Palais Trischli starting the 4th of January 1954 until the 31st. After St. Gallen, I had the month of February booked in a dance hall in Basel called Singerhaus.
